newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: New Austrian chancellor says neutrality to stay.
newsitem.headline: New Austrian chancellor says neutrality to stay.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Viktor Klima, delivering his maiden speech to parliament, stressed on Wednesday there would be no change in the nation's 41-year neutral status without popular support.

"Austrian foreign and security policy has traditionally been determined by consensus. I will aim to pursue this line," said Klima, who formally succeeded Franz Vranitzky as chancellor and Social Democratic Party leader on Tuesday.

European Union membership and the ambitions of neighbouring former Warsaw pact states to join NATO have sparked a lively political debate about neutrality, which is enshrined in Austria's post-World War Two constitution.

The Social Democrats, backed by a clear majority of Austrians, have resisted tampering with the nation's neutral status while the conservative People's Party, junior coalition partner in the two-party government, has indicated it favours NATO membership.
Klima said his government would play an active role in creating a common European security structure but refrained from committing Austria to any one defence alliance.
"It would be unwise to rob ourselves of our room for manoeuvre in such a serious matter and at a time of dynamic change," he said.
